question: What is the thick middle layer of the heart wall called?
explanation: The myocardium is the thick muscular layer responsible for the pumping action of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is the muscular septum between the heart ventricles important?

options.A: It connects the upper atria directly to the lower ventricles
options.B: It produces the lubricating fluid for the pericardial sac
options.C: It stops oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing
options.D: It holds the heart valves firmly in their correct positions

explanation: The septum creates a physical barrier between the left and right sides of the heart to keep pure and impure blood separate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs?
explanation: The right atrium and right ventricle collect blood from the body and send it through the pulmonary circuit to the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient has a weak left ventricle. Which part of the body will immediately suffer from reduced blood supply?
explanation: You've got this! The left ventricle is the powerhouse that pumps oxygenated blood out to feed the entire body, so when it struggles, the systemic circulation feels it right away. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the natural pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The SA node sets the pace of the heart by generating spontaneous electrical impulses. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why does the AV node create a brief delay in the electrical signal?

options.A: To allow the atria to empty blood into the ventricles
options.B: To let the heart muscle rest between fast heart beats
options.C: To send extra blood straight back into the lungs
options.D: To prevent the SA node from firing too many times

explanation: The delay ensures the upper chambers squeeze all their blood down into the ventricles before the ventricles contract. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: What causes the first heart sound, known as "lub"?
explanation: The tricuspid and mitral valves snapping shut at the start of ventricular systole create the first heart sound. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is happening in the heart during ventricular diastole?

options.A: The semilunar valves are forced wide open
options.B: The heart muscle is completely stopped and resting
options.C: The ventricles are relaxing and filling with blood
options.D: The ventricles are squeezing blood into the main arteries

explanation: Diastole is the relaxation phase where heart chambers refill with blood before the next contraction. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: On an ECG tracing, what does the P wave represent?
explanation: Think of the P wave as the electrical wave spreading across the atria right before they squeeze. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which wave on an ECG hides the recovery (repolarization) of the atria?
explanation: The big QRS complex is so electrically loud (representing the ventricles) that it completely hides the smaller wave of atrial recovery. Brilliant clinical detail to know! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)
